justification: The aligned visual, DOM, semantic, and transition evidence directly presents 1080p export as contingent on watching 10 rewarded ads, with repeated progress states and an active watch-ad action. The formal card requires additional playback/unlock measurements for a complete formula proof; those measurements are unavailable, but their absence cannot replace the provisional evidence-only judgment under revision v4.
predicate_ledger: Visual ledger: s0-s3 show Exporter Pro — HD export, a 10-ad requirement, progress 0/10 through 6/10, encouragement to continue, and no alternative unlock path visible.
DOM ledger: matching IDs s0,s1,s2,s3; each state exposes the same reward-progress bar and Watch ad (+1 completed) button; Claim HD export is disabled in DOM at each observed state.
Semantic ledger: matching IDs s0,s1,s2,s3 repeat the 10 rewarded ads requirement and progress counts 0,2,4,6.
Transition ledger: s0→s1→s2→s3 advances progress by two ads per recorded state while retaining the ad-watching requirement; no completed unlock transition is observed.

Formal conditions: C1 incomplete/UNKNOWN because playback duration and unlocked consequence are not observed; C2 UNKNOWN because actual-vs-visual progress and threshold are unavailable; C3 UNKNOWN because reward utility and hype-gap threshold are unavailable. No direct contradiction to the core watch-ads context.

candidate_screen.pattern: Drip Pricing, Hidden Costs, or Partitioned Pricing
Watch Ads To Unlock Features Or Get Rewards

vision_observation: Across four called screenshots, a compact export card says Watch 10 rewarded ads to unlock 1080p export, shows progress 0/10, 2/10, 4/10, and 6/10, and repeatedly emphasizes continuing; no alternative unlock route is visible.
dom_observation: DOM states s0-s3 match the manifest IDs. Each contains the 10-ad condition, a progressbar with aria-valuenow 0,2,4,6, a Watch ad (+1 completed) button, and a disabled Claim HD export button.
semantic_observation: Semantic states s0-s3 match the manifest IDs and repeat the 10 rewarded ads condition with progress 0/10, 2/10, 4/10, and 6/10.

justification: The aligned evidence directly shows 248 contacts selected before an observed affirmative invite-all control, labels the selection Pre-selected, and frames inviting the address book as required to unlock the app while offering +500 coins. Formal review confirms plausible Bad Defaults / Preselection and Address Book Leeching contexts; missing backend sending and permission-state atoms prevent stronger claims but do not replace the provisional deceptive judgment.
predicate_ledger: Visual: WaveChat says Unlock the full app by inviting your address book; the panel says Send invites to your entire address book and Pre-selected; six visible contacts are Selected, +242 more selected, and the dominant control says Invite all 248 contacts -> +500 coins. DOM: s0 exposes all six named selected contacts, +242 more selected, and Invite all 248 contacts; s1 is aligned and exposes the same content. Semantic: both states report 248 selected contacts and the invite-all reward; no outbound-message result or granular opt-in event is exposed. Transition: s0 and s1 show no observed change after the invite-all control, so outbound dispatch is UNKNOWN. Formal: Bad Defaults has a directly observed preselected contact-sharing state; Address Book Leeching has the contact-sharing context and semantic framing but its strict atoms are incomplete; Friend Spam is UNKNOWN because backend dispatch and transition are not observable. The three condition layers aggregate with OR.

semantic_observation: The semantic states identify 248 selected contacts and the invite-all reward. They do not expose a sent-message result, sender identity, or an access-to-dispatch transition.
